title: Orchestration scorecard and escalation scripts (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft for a cross-functional orchestration scorecard and a small set of escalation scripts to be used during incremental activations (microcohorts / microcanaries / A/B slices). The goal: give stewards and oncall a compact, operational summary they can act on quickly, reduce cognitive load during rollouts, and codify decision boundaries that blend safety, latency, and cost.

Audience:
- Rollout stewards (product owners)
- SRE/oncall
- Solutions engineers and SEs running customer pilots
- Observability and telemetry engineers

Scope and assumptions:
- Focused on user-facing LLM features served via Redwood API routing. Includes hosted + dedicated variants.
- Assumes telemetry (latency, errors, token-cost, quality evals) is streaming into Metrics and Traces and that there are synthetic probes available.
- Not a full SOP for legal/privacy; includes quick-notification scripts for T&S and legal when needed.
- This is intentionally compact — detailed runbooks and playbooks live in Confluence (see linked artifacts).

High-level pattern (how to use this doc):
1) Before rollout: owner populates scorecard baseline and registers steward in #deploys slack.
2) During rollout: observe rolling 1m/5m windows; use scorecard to compute an 'activation health' score (see formula).
3) If health < threshold, follow escalation scripts. If health collapse is sudden, immediate rollback.
4) Post-mortem: annotate the scorecard and add any missing telemetry.

Activation health score (compact):
- Inputs (rolling 5m unless noted):
  - p95 latency (s) as LAT_p95
  - error rate (5m) as ERR_5m (server 5xxs + client validation fails)
  - quality-regression vs eval set (24h window) as Q_DELTA (positive means worse)
  - cost-rate change (token cost / minute vs baseline) as COST_DELTA
  - synthetic-signal success rate (end-to-end prompts) as SYN_OK%
- Normalized to 0..1 (lower=bad), weights below approximate initial default:
  - W_LAT = 0.25, W_ERR = 0.30, W_QUAL = 0.25, W_COST = 0.10, W_SYN = 0.10
- Per-metric normalization rules (notes to steward):
  - LAT_score = clamp(1 - (LAT_p95 - baseline_p95)/baseline_p95, 0,1)
  - ERR_score = clamp(1 - ERR_5m/ERR_threshold, 0,1) — ERR_threshold default 0.5% for latency-sensitive features, 1.5% for exploratory features
  - QUAL_score = clamp(1 - (Q_DELTA / 0.02), 0,1) — 2% quality degradation maps to zero
  - COST_score = clamp(1 - min(1, COST_DELTA/0.30), 0,1) — 30% cost drift maps to zero
  - SYN_score = SYN_OK% (0..1) measured from synthetic probes
- Activation_health = weighted_sum(W_x * metric_score) -> 0..1
- Quick decision thresholds (suggested):
  - HEALTH >= 0.85 -> green, continue ramp
  - HEALTH 0.65-0.85 -> yellow, slow ramp + extra sampling + steward check-in
  - HEALTH < 0.65 -> red, invoke escalation script / rollback criteria

Why a composite score:
- Single metric alarms cause thrashing. The composite balances user impact (errors, latency, quality) with economic considerations (cost drift).
- We intentionally lower weight on cost during initial activation; cost matters but not at expense of user experience.

Telemetry & sampling guidance:
- Sampling windows: default 5m rolling, with 1m spikes for automated circuit breakers.
- Breakouts by slice: country, device, user-cohort, routing tier (hosted/dedicated/private)
- Minimum sample size: require at least 100 requests in 5m for the score to be considered stable; otherwise mark as "insufficient data" and use synthetic probes.
- Synthetic probes: 5 canonical prompts covering the top 3 intents + one adversarial prompt; run every 30s per slice during ramp.

Escalation scripts (one-line messages to send during incidents):
- Script A (yellow): "[Activation Yellow] Slice {slice} saw HEALTH={score:.2f} over 5m (lat_p95={lat}ms err={err}%). Slow ramp to 10% and steward pinged. Action: increase sampling & hold escalation window 30m. Link: {link}"
- Script B (red - immediate): "[Activation RED] Slice {slice} HEALTH={score:.2f} (<0.65). Immediate stop & rollback recommended. Sample: lat_p95={lat}ms err={err}%. Oncall: {oncall}. Product steward: {steward}. Runbook: {link}. Initiate rollback in 5m unless command to continue."
- Script C (safety/legal hit): "[Safety Escalation] Unusual generation or TOS risk detected for slice {slice}. Pause activation ASAP. Notify Trust & Safety (t-s@redwood) and Legal. Provide sample IDs and request logs. Ticket: {ticket}"
- Where to post: primary channel #deploys; if oncall engaged then create/update incident channel #inc-{shortid}.

Operator quick checklist (pre-activation):
- Owner checklist (product): confirm evaluation set + golden probes uploaded (link).
- SRE checklist: verify autoscaling and capacity headroom >= 30% for initial ramp; confirm synthetic probe runner active.
- Observability: ensure dashboards exist for p95/p50, error-rate, cost-by-token, eval-quality trend; hook alerts to the scorecard job.
- Compliance: confirm data retention and privacy flags for this model variant; if customer-specific data is present escalate to legal pre-approval.
- Rollback target: confirm previous stable model/config exists and can be reactivated in <5m via routing toggle.

Stewardship roles & rotations (template):
- Steward (owner) = product lead for feature. Responsibilities: hypothesis, traffic schedule, gating thresholds, final go/no-go.
- Oncall SRE = executes rollback, capacity actions, triage perf regressions.
- Observability contact = ensures signals are visible and not noisy.
- Solutions/SEs = customer-facing liaison for dedicated/private pilots.
- Rotation note: steward rotates weekly during launch periods; create calendar invite labeled "Steward On-Call" and add to #deploys.

A/B gating decision matrix (compact):
- Metric types: Safety (T&S flags), Reliability (latency & errors), Quality (eval delta), Adoption (CTR/use-rate), Cost
- Gate precedence: Safety > Reliability > Quality > Adoption > Cost
- Default gating rules:
  - If any Safety flag tripped -> immediate pause (no exceptions)
  - If ERR_5m > ERR_threshold * 2 -> pause
